prerequisites: Knowledge of Mechanical Engineering Fundamentals: Manufacturing technology, Materials science, Theory of mechanisms, Strength of materials, Thermal and fluid mechanics engineering, Electrical systems, Industrial control and automation.

Courses providing knowledge and skills: Materials Science, Machine Calculation, Design and Testing, Elasticity and Strength of Materials, Thermal and Fluid Mechanics Engineering, Mechanics, Strength of Materials, Theory of Structures, Theory of Mechanisms.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the fundamentals and basic applications of fluid-mechanics machines, knowing how to apply them to practical situations in industry and other economic sectors, with quality, safety, efficiency and criteria, using the minimum possible resources.
Know, master and apply all concepts related to fluid-mechanics machines to improve their operation and lay the groundwork for future innovations.
Solve problems and practical situations on the various industrial processes of fluid ventilation and pumping and their adaptation to the most common real situations.
Master dimensional analysis and similarity theory and its applications to hydraulic turbines.

Be able to apply the optimal use and employment of fluid-mechanics machines to the various situations, equipment, systems and processes they will encounter in their professional life, both in industry and in other sectors (residential, services, transport, etc.), using minimal resources and seeking intelligent and innovative solutions, leading the process and the search for solutions.
Acquire the foundations for multidisciplinary participation with criteria of leadership, quality design, intelligent teamwork, innovative problem solving, seeking oriented solutions.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanics systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Fluid machines - Introduction and classification of fluid machines
Hydraulic turbomachinery: Generalities - Definition and classification of hydraulic machines
Hydraulic turbomachinery: Pumps - Definition and classification of pumps
Hydraulic turbomachinery: Turbines - Definition and classification of turbines
Fans - Definition and classification of fans
Similarity in turbomachinery - Geometric, kinematic and dynamic similarity
Characteristic curves - Characteristic curves of hydraulic turbomachinery
Obtaining variables for plotting characteristic curves
Relationship between energy production and consumption
Flow regulation in a pumping system
Construction details of a pumping installation
assessment_rules: A minimum of 40% of the total score in written tests must be obtained. If this critical evaluation criterion is not met, the total grade for the course will be 'FAIL', with the resulting score from the sum of all evaluation systems, capped at a maximum of 4.5 points. To ensure complete evaluation for part-time students (recognized as such by the UR), non-recoverable assessment activities will be replaced by equivalent ones, provided the reason for non-completion is the same for which the university granted part-time student status.
